item.title: The case for BCacheFS inclusion in PVE
item.author: invalid@example.com (alexskysilk)
item.dc:creator: alexskysilk
item.content:encoded:
PVE has (and continues to have) a large presence in the homelab/self hosting crowd. The Primary filesystem option employed for single host applications was and is ZFS, due to its robust featureset and code maturity. Yet ZFS's core structural geometry—fixed virtual device (vdev) layouts, rigid pool topologies, and bolt-on workarounds like RAIDZ expansion or special vdevs—shows strain when modern single-node servers mix NVMe, SATA SSDs, and high-capacity hard drives. item.title: PBS 4.2.14 – chunk lock files under /run/proxmox-backup/locks/<store>/.chunks never removed on S3 datastore → kernel slab exhaustion and OOM during GC
item.author: invalid@example.com (sistemisti5)
item.dc:creator: sistemisti5
item.content:encoded:
Hi all,


we are running a secondary PBS used as an offsite copy: an S3-backed datastore filled by a daily pull sync job, with about two months of retention. Garbage collection on this datastore never completes, and the VM eventually runs out of memory. After some investigation, the cause appears to be per-chunk lock files that are created in /run/proxmox-backup (tmpfs) and never removed.
